session_1.speaker: Caroline
session_1.text: Hey Mel! I finally went to the LGBTQ support group yesterday, it was really empowering.

session_1.speaker: Melanie
session_1.text: That is wonderful, Caroline! How did it feel to be around people who understand?

session_1.speaker: Caroline
session_1.text: Honestly it was the first time I did not feel like the odd one out. I am going again next week.

session_1.speaker: Melanie
session_1.text: I spent the morning painting a sunrise over the lake, the colours came out better than I hoped.

session_1.speaker: Caroline
session_1.text: You have to show me. Do you still use the same acrylic set?

session_1.speaker: Melanie
session_1.text: Yes, though I switched to a wider flat brush for the sky, it holds water much better.

session_2.speaker: Melanie
session_2.text: Guess what, I entered the sunrise painting into the county fair and it took second place.

session_2.speaker: Caroline
session_2.text: Second place! That is amazing, Mel. I told you the wider brush was a good idea.

session_2.speaker: Caroline
session_2.text: Meanwhile I started volunteering at the support group as a greeter, I like welcoming the newcomers.

session_2.speaker: Melanie
session_2.text: That suits you. Do you still have time for the pottery class on Thursdays?

session_2.speaker: Caroline
session_2.text: I dropped pottery, the glazing kiln schedule clashed with the greeter shifts.

session_2.speaker: Melanie
session_2.text: Fair enough. I am thinking of trying pottery myself in the autumn.

session_3.speaker: Caroline
session_3.text: Big news, I am moving to Portland in November for a job at the community centre.

session_3.speaker: Melanie
session_3.text: Portland! I will miss our Tuesday coffee, but that role sounds made for you.

session_3.speaker: Melanie
session_3.text: I finally started the pottery class, my first bowl is lopsided but usable.

session_3.speaker: Caroline
session_3.text: Lopsided bowls hold soup just fine. Send a photo before I leave.
